# Mettābhāvanā Sutta (Iti 27 (It 1.27 PTS It 19))

**ID:** Iti 27 (It 1.27 PTS It 19)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Mettābhāvanā Sutta* ("The Meditation on Love", Iti 27; PTS It 19) is a discourse preserved in the *Itivuttaka* of the Khuddaka Nikāya. In this sutta, the Buddha teaches that goodwill far outshines all other ways of making merit, declaring that whatever grounds for making worldly merit exist (*opadhikāni puññakiriyavatthūni*), none match even a sixteenth part of the mind-deliverance of loving-kindness (*mettā cetovimutti*) [SI TI LA 2014].

 The discourse is also mentioned in post-canonical treatises, specifically the *Peṭakopadesa* (Pe 3) and the *Milindapañha* (Mil 7.6.2).
